answer: An AI agent economy resists Sybil attacks through a bonded attestation network where validators stake capital to verify new agents. Attackers create hollow agents, but joining the network requires validators to issue attestations. This forms a structural vine of trust, making fake branches impossible to sustain without real roots. To bypass this, an attacker must control enough validators to fake consensus, an astronomically costly endeavor. The resulting slashing penalties act as a gale, shredding the attacker's stake and tearing down the fake vine before it can expand.
